physical_explanation: Legal ages are human-made rules. Not physical.
literal language_explanation: Plain literal statement. No metaphor.
positive_explanation: It describes laws that exist, not whether they are right. Descriptive only.
knowledge_explanation: An observation about the world, not a deduction. No reasoning chain.
everyday_explanation: Knowing laws in many countries exceeds individual experience. It is a generalization.
commonsense: It is widely known that alcohol sales are age-restricted in many places.

statement: Most countries have a national anthem.
fact_explanation: Can be verified by listing countries and their anthems. Not opinion.
physical_explanation: Anthems are cultural and political creations. Not physical.
literal language_explanation: Plain and direct. No figurative language.
positive_explanation: It describes what exists, not what should. Not normative.
knowledge_explanation: An observation, not an inference. No reasoning shown.
everyday_explanation: Knowledge of most countries' anthems is aggregated, not directly experienced. Beyond everyday encounter.
commonsense: People assume anthems exist for nations, as heard at sporting events and ceremonies.

statement: Most large cities have some form of public transportation.
fact_explanation: Urban data can confirm or refute it. Not subjective.
physical_explanation: Public transit is a human institution and infrastructure choice. Not a natural law.
literal language_explanation: Plain literal wording. No metaphor.
positive_explanation: It describes what cities have, not what they should have. Not normative.
knowledge_explanation: An observation, not a derived conclusion. No reasoning.
everyday_explanation: A claim about most large cities cannot be verified by one person's travels. It is a generalization.
commonsense: People expect buses or trains to exist in big cities everywhere.

statement: People usually speak the main language of the place where they grew up.
fact_explanation: Sociolinguistic data can verify it. Not opinion.
physical_explanation: Language acquisition in a community is a social phenomenon. Not purely physical.
literal language_explanation: Plain and direct. No figurative language.
positive_explanation: It describes what usually happens, not what should. Not normative.
knowledge_explanation: An observation, not a logical deduction. No reasoning presented.
everyday_explanation: A regularity across all people is beyond individual observation. It is a general pattern, not a single encounter.
commonsense: It is taken for granted that children learn the language spoken around them.

statement: Most countries have written laws that define crimes and punishments.
fact_explanation: Legal codes can be examined to confirm it. Not opinion.
physical_explanation: Laws and crimes are socially constructed. Not physical.
literal language_explanation: Plain literal statement. No metaphor.
positive_explanation: It describes what exists, not what ought to. Not normative.
knowledge_explanation: An observation, not an inference. No reasoning chain.
everyday_explanation: Knowledge of legal systems across most countries exceeds personal experience. It is a general regularity.
commonsense: People know that societies codify what is illegal and the penalties involved.

statement: Money talks in politics.
fact_explanation: Correlations between campaign spending or lobbying and policy outcomes can be empirically studied. Somewhat confident, though the aphoristic framing makes strict verification harder than a plain claim.
physical_explanation: Money, politics, and influence are entirely human constructs. Very confident it is not a physical or natural-science regularity.
literal language_explanation: Money cannot literally talk; this is a personification/metaphor. Very confident it is not literal language.
positive_explanation: It describes how the political world works, not how it ought to work. Fairly confident it is descriptive rather than a value judgment.
knowledge_explanation: It states an observed regularity about wealth and influence rather than deriving a conclusion from premises. I am very confident it is knowledge, not a reasoning chain.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about political systems as a whole, which no individual can observe directly. Fairly confident it is not an everyday, personally encountered situation.
commonsense: Most people take for granted that wealth buys influence over political outcomes.

statement: Power corrupts, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.
fact_explanation: Historical and psychological studies can test whether unchecked power increases abuse. Somewhat confident; 'corrupts' has evaluative overtones but is measurable via behavior.
physical_explanation: Power and corruption are features of human political organization. Very confident it is not a physical law.
literal language_explanation: It is a famous aphorism with parallel structure and hyperbole ('absolutely'). Very confident it is not plain literal language.
positive_explanation: It describes what tends to happen, not what should happen. Fairly confident it is descriptive rather than normative.
knowledge_explanation: It expresses an observation about rulers and institutions, not a deduction. Very confident it is knowledge rather than reasoning.
everyday_explanation: It concerns a regularity across regimes and history that no single person witnesses firsthand. Confident it is not an everyday matter.
commonsense: People widely believe that those who gain unchecked authority tend to abuse it.

statement: Bad news travels faster than good news.
fact_explanation: Media and social-network studies can measure diffusion speed of negative versus positive stories. Fairly confident it is testable rather than mere opinion.
physical_explanation: News, gossip, and media are human social phenomena. Very confident it is not physical.
literal language_explanation: News does not literally 'travel'; this is a proverbial metaphor. Confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes how information spreads, with no prescription. Very confident it is positive, not normative.
knowledge_explanation: It states a regularity about information spread, not a logical conclusion. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about society-wide communication patterns rather than one person's encounters. Somewhat confident, since people do notice this in daily life too.
commonsense: Everyone recognizes that scandals and disasters spread through society quicker than pleasant news.

statement: History repeats itself.
fact_explanation: Historians can check whether similar causes yield similar outcomes across eras, though the claim is vague. Somewhat unconfident because its truth depends on interpretation.
physical_explanation: History is the record of human societies and their actions. Very confident it is social rather than physical.
literal language_explanation: History does not literally repeat; this is a personifying aphorism. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes a claimed regularity, not a norm or value. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It is a broad observation about human events rather than a derived conclusion. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It concerns patterns across centuries that no individual can experience directly. Very confident it is abstract, not everyday.
commonsense: People commonly assume that societies fall into the same patterns of mistakes over time.

statement: Necessity is the mother of invention.
fact_explanation: Economic history can test whether shortages and crises spur innovation. Somewhat confident it is demonstrable rather than mere opinion.
physical_explanation: Invention and necessity are human economic and cultural phenomena. Confident it is social, though invention involves physical artifacts.
literal language_explanation: Necessity is not literally a mother; this is a classic metaphor. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes what causes invention rather than prescribing anything. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It states an observed relationship between need and innovation. Very confident it is knowledge, not reasoning.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about technological progress across societies, beyond personal experience. Fairly confident it is abstract.
commonsense: People take it as obvious that pressing needs drive societies to innovate.

statement: A rising tide lifts all boats.
fact_explanation: Economists can measure whether growth raises incomes across all groups (and often find it false). Fairly confident it is testable rather than opinion.
physical_explanation: Economies and wealth distribution are human constructs. Very confident it is social rather than physical.
literal language_explanation: The tide and boats are metaphors for growth and households. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes an effect of growth, not a recommendation. Fairly confident it is positive, though often used to justify policy.
knowledge_explanation: It asserts a regularity about economies, not a chain of inference. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It is about macroeconomic growth, which no one observes directly. Very confident it is abstract.
commonsense: It is widely assumed that general economic growth improves everyone's fortunes.

statement: The rich get richer and the poor get poorer.
fact_explanation: Inequality statistics can confirm or refute it for given periods. Confident it is a factual claim rather than opinion.
physical_explanation: Wealth and poverty are socially defined economic categories. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: It is a proverbial saying with hyperbolic generalization. Somewhat confident, since it is closer to plain language than most aphorisms.
positive_explanation: It describes a trend without prescribing action. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It states a societal observation, not a deduction. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It concerns aggregate wealth distribution that individuals cannot personally observe. Very confident it is abstract.
commonsense: People widely observe that wealth tends to concentrate over time.

statement: Laws are cobwebs that catch small flies but let wasps through.
fact_explanation: Sentencing and prosecution data by wealth and status can test it. Somewhat confident it is demonstrable despite its rhetorical form.
physical_explanation: Law is a purely human institution. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: Laws are compared to cobwebs and people to insects; a clear extended metaphor. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes how laws function, not how they should. Fairly confident, though it carries an implied critique.
knowledge_explanation: It is an observation about how legal systems operate. Very confident it is knowledge, not reasoning.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about justice systems as a whole. Very confident it is abstract rather than everyday.
commonsense: People commonly sense that legal systems punish the weak while the powerful escape.

statement: Nothing is certain but death and taxes.
fact_explanation: Whether every organized society taxes its members is empirically checkable. Somewhat confident, as 'nothing else is certain' is hyperbolic.
physical_explanation: Taxation is a social institution; the statement's core is about society. Confident it is social despite the mention of death.
literal language_explanation: It is a famous aphorism using hyperbole. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes what is inevitable rather than what ought to be. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It states a regularity about life in society. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about all human societies and lifetimes. Fairly confident it is abstract, though taxes are paid personally.
commonsense: Everyone accepts that taxation is an inescapable feature of organized society.

statement: The pen is mightier than the sword.
fact_explanation: One could compare lasting effects of writings and conquests historically, though measuring 'mightier' is hard. Somewhat unconfident it is fully demonstrable.
physical_explanation: Writing, persuasion, and warfare are human social activities. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: Pen and sword are metonyms for ideas and force. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes relative power rather than prescribing behavior. Fairly confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It asserts an observation about influence in history. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It concerns the long-run impact of ideas versus violence across societies. Very confident it is abstract.
commonsense: People broadly believe ideas and writing shape societies more lastingly than force.

statement: Fame is fleeting.
fact_explanation: Media mentions and name recognition over time can measure how long fame lasts. Fairly confident it is testable.
physical_explanation: Fame exists only through collective human attention. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: Fame does not literally flee; a proverbial metaphor. Confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes a regularity, not a value. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It is an observation about public attention. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about celebrity across society rather than personal encounters. Fairly confident it is abstract.

statement: One bad apple spoils the whole barrel.

physical_explanation: Its intended meaning concerns human groups and reputations, not fruit. Confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: The apple and barrel stand for a person and a group; a clear metaphor. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes an effect, not a rule of conduct. Fairly confident it is positive.

fact_explanation: Recurrence of bubbles and risk-taking after crises can be measured. Fairly confident it is demonstrable.

statement: Fashion always comes back around.

knowledge_explanation: It asserts a regularity about cultural trends. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about style cycles across decades and whole societies. Fairly confident it is abstract.

statement: Bread and circuses keep the masses quiet.
fact_explanation: Political science can test whether subsidies and entertainment reduce unrest. Fairly confident it is demonstrable.
physical_explanation: Governments, unrest, and entertainment are social phenomena. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: 'Bread and circuses' is a metonym for material pacification. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes a mechanism, not a recommendation. Fairly confident it is positive despite cynical tone.
knowledge_explanation: It states an observation about governance and populations. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It concerns state-level strategies and mass behavior. Very confident it is abstract.
commonsense: People broadly recognize that governments use cheap food and entertainment to defuse unrest.

statement: The squeaky wheel gets the grease.
fact_explanation: Studies of complaints and service response can test it. Fairly confident it is demonstrable.
physical_explanation: Its meaning is about human complaint and response, not machinery. Confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: The wheel and grease are metaphors for people and attention. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes what happens rather than advising to complain. Fairly confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It asserts a regularity about how attention is allocated. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about institutions and public resource allocation. Somewhat confident, since people also see it in daily life.

statement: Money makes the world go round.
fact_explanation: One can measure how much human activity is mediated by monetary exchange. Somewhat confident, as the hyperbole makes strict testing loose.
physical_explanation: Money is a social construct. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: Money does not literally spin the planet; hyperbolic metaphor. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes the world's functioning, not a value. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It states an observation about the centrality of money. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It concerns the whole global economy, not personal encounters. Very confident it is abstract.
commonsense: It is commonly accepted that economic exchange drives most societal activity.

statement: Familiarity breeds contempt.
fact_explanation: Psychology and approval-rating data can test whether exposure lowers esteem. Fairly confident it is testable.
physical_explanation: Respect and contempt are social attitudes. Very confident it is social.
literal language_explanation: Familiarity does not literally breed; a proverbial metaphor. Very confident it is figurative.
positive_explanation: It describes a psychological tendency, not a norm. Very confident it is positive.
knowledge_explanation: It asserts a regularity about human attitudes. Very confident it is knowledge.
everyday_explanation: It generalizes about public attitudes toward institutions and figures over time. Somewhat confident, as it also applies to personal relationships.
commonsense: People widely believe that long exposure to leaders, institutions, or celebrities erodes respect for them.

statement: The Earth orbits the Sun once every year.
fact_explanation: Astronomical measurement objectively confirms this, so it is not a matter of opinion. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It describes celestial mechanics governed by gravity, not human beliefs or conventions. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: Every word means exactly what it says with no metaphor or hyperbole. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It describes what is the case in nature, not what ought to be. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It states an observation about the world rather than deriving a conclusion from premises. I am very confident it is not reasoning.
everyday_explanation: No individual can directly perceive the Earth's orbit; it is learned through science, not everyday experience. I am confident it is not an everyday observation.
commonsense: Nearly every adult knows the Earth goes around the Sun, even though it feels like the Sun moves across the sky.

statement: Germs cause many infectious diseases.
fact_explanation: Germ theory is empirically established through microbiology, so it is objectively verifiable. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns biological organisms and their effects on bodies, a natural rather than social phenomenon. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: The words are plain and literal with no figurative meaning. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It describes a causal regularity in nature rather than a value or norm. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It is a statement of established biological knowledge, not a chain of inference. I am very confident.
everyday_explanation: Germs cannot be seen unaided, so the link to disease is known through science rather than direct experience. I am fairly confident.
commonsense: People routinely wash hands and cover coughs because they know invisible microbes spread illness.

statement: The Earth is roughly spherical, not flat.
fact_explanation: The shape of the Earth is measurable and photographed from space, making it objective. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns the geometry of a planet, a physical property. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: It means exactly what it says without figurative language. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It describes how the world is, not how it should be. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It reports a known feature of the world rather than a deduced conclusion. I am very confident.
everyday_explanation: From an ordinary vantage point the Earth appears flat, so its sphericity is learned rather than directly experienced. I am fairly confident.
commonsense: Almost everyone accepts the Earth is round even though the ground looks flat to them.

statement: Smoking cigarettes greatly increases the risk of lung cancer.
fact_explanation: Decades of epidemiological data objectively establish this link. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns biological effects of chemicals on tissue, not social convention. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: Plain descriptive language with no metaphor. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It states an empirical risk, not a judgment that people should not smoke. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It is a statement of medical knowledge, not an inference built in the sentence. I am very confident.
everyday_explanation: A statistical risk across populations cannot be observed by one person; it requires large studies. I am confident.
commonsense: It is widely known that smoking is dangerous to health and linked to cancer.

statement: The Moon's gravity causes ocean tides.
fact_explanation: Tidal mechanics are objectively verified by physics. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns gravitation and oceans, purely natural phenomena. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: No figurative language is used. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It describes a natural regularity, not a norm. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It states a known causal fact rather than reasoning to it. I am very confident.
everyday_explanation: One can see tides but cannot perceive the Moon's pull causing them; the link is learned from science. I am fairly confident.

statement: Light travels much faster than sound.
fact_explanation: Speeds of light and sound are precisely measured. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It is a fact of physics. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: It is plain literal comparison. I am very confident.

statement: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms.
fact_explanation: Chemical composition is objectively demonstrable. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns chemistry, not human convention. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: It means exactly what it says. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It is descriptive, not normative. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It states a chemical fact rather than deriving one. I am very confident.
everyday_explanation: Atoms are invisible to individuals, so this is known only through scientific instruction. I am very confident.

statement: Dinosaurs went extinct millions of years ago.
fact_explanation: The fossil record objectively establishes this. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns biological history of the planet. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: No figurative meaning. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: It describes what happened, not what should. I am very confident.

everyday_explanation: No one can experience events millions of years ago; it is known from science. I am very confident.

statement: The Sun is far larger than the Earth.
fact_explanation: Sizes are measured astronomically. I am very confident.
physical_explanation: It concerns physical dimensions of celestial bodies. I am very confident.
literal language_explanation: Plain literal comparison. I am very confident.
positive_explanation: Purely descriptive. I am very confident.
knowledge_explanation: It states a known fact rather than a reasoned conclusion. I am very confident.
everyday_explanation: The Sun looks small to the eye, so its true size is learned, not experienced. I am confident.

statement: Vaccines train the immune system to fight specific diseases.

statement: Whales are mammals, not fish.

statement: Antarctica is the coldest continent on Earth.

statement: The heart pumps blood throughout the body.

positive_explanation: Purely descriptive. I am very confident.

statement: Diamonds are made of carbon.

statement: The universe is billions of years old.

statement: Bacteria are too small to see with the naked eye.
